Simple Circulation (C-M-C): A seller exchanges a
commodity for money to buy a different commodity
for consumption. The goal is use value. The
money stays in circulation.
Capitalist Totality (M-C-M'): The capitalist
advances money to buy commodities, only to sell
them for more money. The goal is the continuous,
conscious expansion of exchange value.
The Core Mystery
If commodities are exchanged at their true value, where does the extra value (+) at the end of the
loop come from? Circulation alone cannot create value ex nihilo.

The Engine of Surplus Value
The capitalist pays the worker a wage equal to the cost of their survival (Variable Capital).
But the capitalist consumes the worker's actual living labor for the entire day.

The Continuous Engine of Reproduction
The result of capitalist production is not just commodities and profit. It is the
reproduction of the social relationship itself.
THE SUPERSTRUCTURE
The Trap: The worker consumes their
wage to survive, returning to the
market the next day with nothing but
their capacity to work, exactly as
before.
The Superstructure: The surplus
product extracted from the worker
becomes the material base that
funds the "free time" of non-working
classes, the State, art, and science
Ejected to
Exteriority
The Coercion: No external force is
needed. The worker is bound by

that alienates them.

The Ethical Metaphysics of Marx
For Enrique Dussel, Marx's economic manuscripts are not
merely a science of the Totality of capital.
They are
a profound "Philosophy of Liberation" rooted in the
Exteriority of the human being.
- Capital is an ontology of the Same-a closed system of dead,
objectified labor expanding infinitely.
True reality, and the source of all value, lies outside this system in
the living, breathing, suffering corporality of the worker
- Marx's critique is ultimately an ethical defense of the absolute,
transcendent dignity of Living Labor against its reduction to a mere
internal gear of the machine.
